CKP, is a generalization of the Knapsack Problem, which involves selecting items from multiple groups, where each item has a unique value and weight, and the total weight of selected items from each group cannot exceed a given capacity. CKP is a special case of this problem, where selected items from each group are complementary, meaning if one item is chosen, the rest of that group is excluded. CKP is a special case of the Weighted Independent Set Problem on a particular graph type, known as a circle graph. This paper presents a new exact algorithm for CKP, which uses a branch-and-bound method, and shows that it performs better than a previously used branch-and-bound approach for the Weighted Independent Set Problem on a circle graph. The algorithm was tested on a large set of CKP instances, and it was found to solve all instances within a reasonable time frame, and outperforms the previously used branch-and-bound approach for the Weighted Independent Set Problem on a circle graph.
